title: Confidently Wrong: Detecting Hallucinations in Financial Question Answering from LLM Internal States
abstract: arXiv:2607.11414v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) in financial applications fail most consequentially when they are confidently wrong. Hedged, uncertain answers invite scrutiny, whereas confident errors silently degrade downstream decisions without warning. We ask how reliably such confidently wrong answers, or confident hallucinations, can be detected from a model's internal activations, and whether those activations carry information beyond its output-level confidence signals. We train linear probes on the residual stream and evaluate them on two established numerical question-answering (QA) benchmarks built from real filings, FinQA and TAT-QA. translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）在金融应用中，最严重的失败情形是“自信却错误”。含糊、不确定的回答会引起人们的审视，而自信的错误却会在毫无预警的情况下悄然损害下游决策。我们探讨如何从模型的内部激活中可靠地检测出这类自信却错误的回答（即“自信幻觉”），以及这些激活是否包含超出模型输出层面置信信号之外的信息。我们在残差流上训练线性探针，并在两个基于真实财报构建的成熟数值问答基准——FinQA和TAT-QA上对其进行评估。行为置信度通过同一问题的八个重采样回答之间的一致性来衡量，并将探针的有效性与基线方法进行比较，例如token对数概率以及模型对自身答案的真/假自评。我们的研究结果表明，在自信的回答中，那些……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出在大语言模型残差流上训练线性探针，利用模型内部激活来检测金融问答中“自信却错误”的幻觉回答，并证明内部状态包含超越输出层面置信度信号（如token对数概率和模型自我真/假评估）的判别信息。
en_tdlr: This paper trains linear probes on LLM residual streams to detect confidently wrong hallucinations in financial question answering, showing that internal activations carry discriminative information beyond output-level confidence signals such as token log-probabilities and the model's own True/False self-assessment.
